reasoning_traces.think:
The temporal grounding pipeline operates in four stages: (1) semantic region-of-interest (ROI) detection using a fine-tuned YOLOv8l model to identify scorebug elements such as quarter and time-remaining; (2) optical character recognition (OCR) via PaddleOCR to extract textual values from these regions; (3) denoising and interpolation using a linear clock trend model to fill gaps in detected times; and (4) parallelized frame processing for scalability. The core mathematical operation is a linear interpolation T = T₀ − (1/30)·n, where T is the estimated time remaining, T₀ is the initial time at the start of a period, and n is the number of frames elapsed. Confidence gates ensure only high-quality detections are accepted, defined by C = Pr(object) × IoU > T. This pipeline assumes static ROIs and a linear clock trend, making it robust to minor occlusions but sensitive to missing or inconsistent scorebugs. Failure modes include unreliable OCR in low-contrast environments or non-linear clock behavior during ad breaks. The method's strength lies in its adaptability across broadcasters due to its generic training on multiple leagues, though it requires reannotation for NFL-specific scorebug dynamics.
